item.title: I attempt to figure out what the heck this thing is
item.content:encoded:
Spoilers?

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-579 is heavily expunged. What’s left, we can maybe figure out.
The containment site’s name (Site-62C) is located 80 km from another site, of redacted number. The destruction and subsequent containment of SCP-004-1 implies that this is to prevent a breach, and that the redacted site is Site-62, with 62C thus being within 004-7’s corresponding dimension. As for why 004-1 must be contained as such, it is likely that 579 is contained for the same reason. 579 is a destroyed doorway. But to what? What is so significant about what is beyond 579 that it must be contained at all costs? We can assume from addendum 579-002 that whatever is being contained, it will likely breach again. From the infohazard tag’s presence, we can tell that 579 is an infohazard. This is going to be a bit of a stretch, but if we take Roget’s Proposal’s cryptic line of 579 and SCP-055’s mutual containment of “Can’t fit round pegs in square holes”, we might have a solution. We know that 055 is not spherical, so it is the square hole, which information falls out of. The round peg is thus either 579 or information on 579. We can thus formulate a tentative description:

SCP-579 is a doorway (presumably a stronger one than wood) of some sort with infohazardous properties. Bad things happen if people know what’s on the other side. This effect was previously mitigated by SCP-055’s presence nearby.

Welp, there ya have it. Not much, but it’s more description than an expungement. We then understand why it must be contained this way. It is to prevent the doorway from opening, to suppress all information.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I honestly don’t understand why people hate this SCP so much. It’s one of the most carefully-written on the entire site.

The content of this article matches the SCP format in a way that SCP articles inherently demand - not to get too literary theory here, but the point is that in a canon where Dangerous Hidden Stuff exists in a manner that make it a must to have it be contained, there must be a reference point. 579 is that point.

With 579, you know more about what you don’t know than what you actually know. It’s not that this is supposed to be inherently terrifying or anything, it just tells a story differently than most other SCPs.

I think a lot of people have the problem that it isn’t described as dangerous, believing that this makes it rather pointless without meta-reason for it. Honestly that’s not the point. The danger is implied because we know what SCPs are like and what Keter means. But if that’s all the implied data you take, you’re missing out.

The implications in how it’s stored and the sheer length of the containment timeline and the fact that only 7 surviving people know what it is, and that it isn’t a concern that they do know, together exist to show you that it’s important without telling you so. The idea that, after they seal it in another dimension, they’ll reveal what it is also implies that, because the data isn’t out yet, it’s still in containment - but only barely, given the precision of the containment procedures. It’s a sword of Damocles, like that paradoxical insurance policy, but shadowy-implicit.

The ability to do this takes a lot of good writing skills because the author clearly is aware of what the reader expects from SCP and plays with those expectations by giving enough information to imply danger while using enough redaction to imply a dramatic scale, despite what appear to be statements to the contrary.

We need more SCPs with this amount of thought put into the metanarrative of SCP articles as a whole.

item.title: This could be improved with [DATA EXPUNGED]
item.content:encoded:
What do you mean, the title is unfinished? I clearly stated that the article could be improved with [DATA EXPUNGED]

I think this SCP is one that simply got lucky. Lucky that something like this was considered "good" at the time.

I don't know what the author was envisioning when they were writing this, but to me it just seems like they were too lazy or too indecisive on the details.

With this one, I feel they used the [DATA EXPUNGED] format just for the sake of using it. What is it? Nobody knows! Not even the author!

And no, I don't think it being a "supermemetic" is a good excuse. If we can have containment procedures for all sorts of memetic SCPs, and even one for an antimemetic like SCP-3125, there's no reason we can't contain this.

Don't get me wrong, I think the wiki needs a SCP like this, even if it's just to show a format that's "different." It used the [DATA EXPUNGED] format and went bonkers with it.

But that doesn't mean I have to like it. This SCP should be moved to a separate page, just to preserve it. It deserves recognition, but not an SCP title.

SCP-835 is one of my personal favorites because it shows how messed up things hiding under the [REDACTED] sign can be. The author actually knew what they were going to put there, and used the format accordingly.

But the gist of this format is just the format itself.

So, until the shroud of [DATA EXPUNGED] is removed, a solid -1 for me.

item.content:encoded:
Destroying 004-1 is actually consistent with Special Containment Procedures for 004 - any event wherein an object breaches containment of 004 is grounds for detonating the on-site nuclear warhead. Due to its implied properties, SCP-579 is very likely to breach containment of SCP-004, so destroying the door prematurely makes sense. Therefore, it doesn't read as gratuitous shock value for me.

Anyway, the controversy of expunging a description aside, I think this article is fine. It tells a logical story, and the description being expunged can be justified in the context of the universe (e.g. this is the document given to Level 1 personnel assigned to SCP-579).

+ If we're going to theorize:
If we're going to theorize:


If we're going to theorize, it seems like describing SCP-579 in any capacity causes it to change its attributes (size, location, even hostility) to contradict that description. This is why all its attributes must be measured in real-time. This is also why the entire Description is expunged; it gives the Foundation a buffer to describe things like Special Containment Procedures without directly referencing the object itself.

Further, it cannot revert its attributes to a state that would make previous descriptions about it true. This is why it never can be returned to its previous containment sites or its Point of Origin. (So why not just call it "dangerous" so that it stops being dangerous? Easy - the Foundation probably initially classed SCP-579 as "Safe.")

If SCP-579 is irresistibly forced to contradict its own rules, the object takes action to prevent that contradiction - destroying its Point of Origin, for example, after repeated attempts to return it there.

It took the Foundation a while to realize this, so the object kept escaping containment (because they kept noting the site where it was stored - this is also why information about previous sites of containment isn't expunged; because it's pointless to do so) until it was moved to a redacted location that has not been described. Containment procedure hinges upon not describing the object.

This is also why the Foundation is tracking any mention of SCP-579, anywhere - because this means the risk that someone might describe it and cause a containment breach is much higher. They specifically name "anti-Foundation" groups because it would be easy for an anti-Foundation group to use this against them. For example, they could state "SCP-579 will not terminate all Foundation personnel." And then it does.

Action-Israfil-A most likely consists of an attempt by Site personnel to recapture the object using the magnets in the 30m x 30m x 30m room, at a slightly different position. This is more of a Hail Mary attempt than anything else - that's why they're only given seven minutes to do so before Action-Israfil-B begins.

Action-Israfil-B is damage control, only. That's why it involves basically locking SCP-579 in another dimension (if possible). If SCP-579 breaches containment, the likelihood of more destructive events due to its properties would increase as more people attempt to describe the object and create more contradictory conditions for it. That's how 579 is capable of apocalyptic-level events.

The Foundation estimates that they have about 1 year to execute similar contingency plans they would apply to general XK-Class scenarios.

Anyway, obviously this is a pretty engaging object, so I'd call it a success. +1

item.content:encoded:
I actually had to read this twice to "get" it. At first, I understood this was going for something mysterious, but it felt more like "This is something. If this something does something, then you need to do something. If that something fails, do something."

On re-reading, the containment options feel more clear (Maybe I was just too tired when I first read it, though), and "Destroy the whole site!" does imply fairly well how dangerous that thing is.
That said, while I get why others would like it, I think it remains a little bit too mysterious for me to be scary. While lockdown and then destruction shows the danger, it still feels comparably "tame", in a way.
For example, SCP-231 also goes with the more mysterious approach, as all we know is it's a little pregnant girl, and whatever she's pregnant with is dangerous as hell - Not much more than we know about 579. However, 579's containment procedures amount to "Check data; if the data isn't right, go into lockdown; if the data still isn't right after a set amount of time, destroy the site." 231's, on the other hand, we don't even know. We know just enough to understand it's awful, bad enough that one little committed suicide, and several personnel requested amnestics because it was so bad. That's terrifying. It may not be worse objectively (Death of many personnel due to the destruction is, objectively, fairly bad), but emotions don't work objectively. Just like nobody cares about hundreds of red shirts dying, but one of the heroes dying makes us cry. "Lockdown and destroy" doesn't scare us unless there's someone in there we care about, but "do something unspeakably horrible to a little child" does, since our instincts tell us to protect children.

Sorry if I was rambling ^^" Just trying to explain how I feel about this SCP.
